from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Foundation: Prerequisite - What is a Slope?"
        lines = [
            "Meet Turbo, a snail crawling up a plank.",
            "Every meter forward, he rises two meters.",
            "This constant rate of change is the slope."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Display coordinate grid with blue line y=2x
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 3, 1],
            y_range=[0, 5, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY},
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "F6")
        
        # y = 2x line in Blue (#0000FF)
        line = axes.plot(lambda x: 2 * x, x_range=[0, 2], color="#0000FF")
        
        # Turbo the snail (represented by a snail-like dot/icon)
        turbo = Dot(color=WHITE, radius=0.1)
        turbo_label = Text("Turbo", font_size=16).next_to(turbo, UP, buff=0.1)
        turbo_group = VGroup(turbo, turbo_label)
        turbo_group.move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(line), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(turbo_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Update highlighting
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Move Turbo from (0,0) to (1,2)
        # Use an updater to keep the label with the dot
        def update_label(m):
            m.next_to(turbo, UP, buff=0.1)
            
        turbo_label.add_updater(update_label)
        
        self.play(turbo.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(1, 2)), run_time=2)
        turbo_label.remove_updater(update_label)
        
        # Draw red (#FF0000) triangle highlighting Rise=2, Run=1
        p0 = axes.c2p(0, 0)
        p1 = axes.c2p(1, 0)
        p2 = axes.c2p(1, 2)
        
        run_line = Line(p0, p1, color="#FF0000")
        rise_line = Line(p1, p2, color="#FF0000")
        run_label = Text("Run=1", font_size=14, color="#FF0000").next_to(run_line, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        rise_label = Text("Rise=2", font_size=14, color="#FF0000").next_to(rise_line, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        triangle = VGroup(run_line, rise_line, run_label, rise_label)
        
        self.play(Create(triangle), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Update highlighting
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Show 'Slope = 2' in yellow next to triangle
        slope_text = Text("Slope = 2", color="#FFFF00", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(slope_text, "D5")
        
        self.play(Write(slope_text))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Morph the line into a white parabola
        parabola = axes.plot(lambda x: x**2, x_range=[0, 2.2], color=WHITE)
        
        # Mark a point with a blinking green (#00FF00) dot
        blink_dot = Dot(axes.c2p(1.5, 2.25), color="#00FF00")
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(triangle),
            FadeOut(turbo_group),
            FadeOut(slope_text),
            Transform(line, parabola),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Blinking effect for the green dot
        self.add(blink_dot)
        for _ in range(3):
            self.play(blink_dot.animate.set_opacity(0), run_time=0.3)
            self.play(blink_dot.animate.set_opacity(1), run_time=0.3)
            
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize the layout with title and lecture lines
        lecture_lines = [
            "Zoom into a point on this rollercoaster track.",
            "The smooth curve eventually looks perfectly straight.",
            "This is the tangent line at that point.",
            "The line's steepness is the derivative."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Geometric Intuition: Local Linearity", lecture_lines)
        
        # Ensure UI elements stay on top of the zooming graph
        self.lecture.set_z_index(10)
        self.title.set_z_index(10)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-0.2, 2.2, 1],
            y_range=[-0.2, 4.2, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=5,
            axis_config={"color": BLUE_E, "include_tip": False}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A3', 'F6')
        
        parabola = axes.plot(lambda x: x**2, x_range=[0, 2.1], color=WHITE)
        # Point P at (1,1)
        p_coords = axes.c2p(1, 1)
        dot = Dot(p_coords, color=WHITE, radius=0.08)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(parabola), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(dot))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Tangent line at x=1: y = 2x - 1
        tangent = axes.plot(lambda x: 2*x - 1, x_range=[0.4, 1.6], color="#FFD700")
        self.play(Create(tangent))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Group components for a unified zoom effect
        zoom_group = VGroup(axes, parabola, tangent, dot)
        zoom_center = dot.get_center()
        
        # Execute the zoom. We also adjust stroke widths to prevent excessive thickness.
        self.play(
            zoom_group.animate.scale(20, about_point=zoom_center),
            parabola.animate.set_stroke_width(2),
            tangent.animate.set_stroke_width(2),
            axes.animate.set_stroke_width(1),
            dot.animate.scale(0.1), # Keep dot size reasonable relative to zoom
            run_time=4
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700") 
        
        self.play(Indicate(tangent, color="#FFD700", scale_factor=1.05))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        label = Text("Local Linearity", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        # Position near the zoomed center
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'E5', scale_factor=1.2)
        label.set_z_index(10)
        
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.wait(3)

        # Final state cleanup
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title and Lecture Lines
        title = "The Power Rule: The Geometry of Growing Squares"
        lines = [
            "Imagine a square with side length x.",
            "When x grows slightly, the area increases.",
            "Two thin strips are added to the edges.",
            "The power rule calculates this growth rate: 2x."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        BLUE_STRIP = "#ADD8E6"
        RED_CORNER = "#FF0000"
        GROWTH_COLOR = "#FFFF00"

        # Define sizes relative to grid units (1 unit per grid cell)
        square_side = 2.0
        dx = 0.3

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Create Main Square
        main_square = Square(side_length=square_side, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        self.place_in_area(main_square, "C2", "D3")
        
        # Use MarkupText to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        area_label = MarkupText("x<sup>2</sup>", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(area_label, "C2", "D3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        side_x_bottom = Text("x", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(side_x_bottom, "E2", scale_factor=0.7)
        side_x_bottom.shift(RIGHT * 0.5) 
        
        side_x_left = Text("x", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(side_x_left, "C1", scale_factor=0.7)
        side_x_left.shift(DOWN * 0.5) 
        
        self.play(Create(main_square), Write(area_label))
        self.play(Write(side_x_bottom), Write(side_x_left))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE_STRIP)
        )
        
        dx_label_top = Text("dx", color=BLUE_STRIP)
        self.place_at_grid(dx_label_top, "B2", scale_factor=0.6)
        dx_label_top.shift(RIGHT * 0.5)

        dx_label_right = Text("dx", color=BLUE_STRIP)
        self.place_at_grid(dx_label_right, "C4", scale_factor=0.6)
        dx_label_right.shift(DOWN * 0.5)

        self.play(Write(dx_label_top), Write(dx_label_right))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE_STRIP)
        )

        top_strip = Rectangle(width=square_side, height=dx, color=BLUE_STRIP, fill_opacity=0.5, stroke_width=1)
        right_strip = Rectangle(width=dx, height=square_side, color=BLUE_STRIP, fill_opacity=0.5, stroke_width=1)
        corner_square = Square(side_length=dx, color=RED_CORNER, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=1)

        top_strip.next_to(main_square, UP, buff=0)
        right_strip.next_to(main_square, RIGHT, buff=0)
        corner_square.next_to(right_strip, UP, buff=0)

        self.play(
            FadeIn(top_strip, shift=UP*0.1),
            FadeIn(right_strip, shift=RIGHT*0.1)
        )
        self.play(Create(corner_square))
        
        strip_label_1 = Text("x · dx", color=BLUE_STRIP)
        self.place_at_grid(strip_label_1, "B3", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        strip_label_2 = Text("x · dx", color=BLUE_STRIP)
        self.place_at_grid(strip_label_2, "D4", scale_factor=0.5)
        strip_label_2.rotate(-PI/2)

        corner_label = MarkupText("dx<sup>2</sup>", color=RED_CORNER)
        self.place_at_grid(corner_label, "B4", scale_factor=0.4)

        self.play(Write(strip_label_1), Write(strip_label_2))
        self.play(Write(corner_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GROWTH_COLOR)
        )

        growth_text = Text("Total Growth ≈ 2x · dx", color=GROWTH_COLOR, font_size=24)
        self.place_in_area(growth_text, "F1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        power_rule = MarkupText("d/dx(x<sup>2</sup>) = 2x", color=GROWTH_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(power_rule, "E1", "E6", scale_factor=1.1)

        self.play(Write(growth_text))
        self.play(FadeIn(power_rule, shift=UP*0.2))
        
        self.play(
            strip_label_1.animate.set_color(GROWTH_COLOR),
            strip_label_2.animate.set_color(GROWTH_COLOR),
            rate_func=there_and_back
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title and Lecture Lines
        title_text = "Trigonometric Derivatives: The Rhythm of the Circle"
        lecture_lines = [
            "A Ferris wheel rider moves in a circle.",
            "Their vertical position follows a sine wave.",
            "Vertical speed is fastest at the center.",
            "This speed matches the cosine of the angle."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # --- Coordinate System & Objects ---
        # Center the visual logic on C4 area
        radius_val = 1.2
        theta_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        circle = Circle(radius=radius_val, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(circle, "B3", "E5")
        circle_center = circle.get_center()
        
        axes = VGroup(
            Line(circle_center + LEFT * 1.5, circle_center + RIGHT * 1.5, color=GRAY_B, stroke_opacity=0.4),
            Line(circle_center + DOWN * 1.5, circle_center + UP * 1.5, color=GRAY_B, stroke_opacity=0.4)
        )
        
        # Radius line and point (Rider)
        radius_line = always_redraw(lambda: Line(
            circle_center, 
            circle_center + np.array([
                radius_val * np.cos(theta_tracker.get_value()),
                radius_val * np.sin(theta_tracker.get_value()),
                0
            ]),
            color=WHITE
        ))
        
        rider = always_redraw(lambda: Dot(
            circle_center + np.array([
                radius_val * np.cos(theta_tracker.get_value()),
                radius_val * np.sin(theta_tracker.get_value()),
                0
            ]), 
            color=WHITE,
            radius=0.08
        ))
        
        # Green sine line (vertical height)
        sine_line = always_redraw(lambda: Line(
            circle_center + np.array([radius_val * np.cos(theta_tracker.get_value()), 0, 0]),
            circle_center + np.array([
                radius_val * np.cos(theta_tracker.get_value()),
                radius_val * np.sin(theta_tracker.get_value()),
                0
            ]),
            color="#00FF00",
            stroke_width=6
        ))

        # Blue cosine vector (horizontal coordinate representing rate of vertical change)
        cosine_vector = always_redraw(lambda: Arrow(
            circle_center,
            circle_center + np.array([radius_val * np.cos(theta_tracker.get_value()), 0, 0]),
            color="#0000FF",
            buff=0,
            stroke_width=4,
            max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.2
        ))

        # Formulas and Labels - Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid LaTeX dependency
        sin_label = Text("sin(θ)", color="#00FF00", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(sin_label, "B5")
        
        cos_label = Text("cos(θ)", color="#0000FF", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(cos_label, "E5")
        
        deriv_formula = Text("d/dθ sin(θ) = cos(θ)", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(deriv_formula, "F4")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "A Ferris wheel rider moves in a circle."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE_A)
        self.add(axes, circle, radius_line, rider)
        self.play(theta_tracker.animate.set_value(PI/6), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Their vertical position follows a sine wave."
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.add(sine_line)
        self.play(Write(sin_label))
        self.play(theta_tracker.animate.set_value(PI/3), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Vertical speed is fastest at the center."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Loop through a full rotation to observe sine/cosine dynamics
        self.play(theta_tracker.animate.set_value(2.5 * PI), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "This speed matches the cosine of the angle."
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#0000FF")
        self.add(cosine_vector)
        self.play(Write(cos_label))
        self.play(Write(deriv_formula))
        # Final rotation highlighting the relationship
        self.play(theta_tracker.animate.set_value(4.5 * PI), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2)

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        lecture_lines = [
            "Formulas provide shortcuts for finding local steepness.",
            "They let us predict how dynamic systems change.",
            "Now you have the intuition to master calculus!"
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary: The Speedometer of Change", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Simultaneously draw a white curve on the left and a speedometer on the right.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # 1. Curve Setup (using Axes for local coordinates)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=3,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"color": GREY_B, "include_tip": False}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F3")
        
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: x**2, x_range=[-1.5, 1.5], color=WHITE)
        curve_label = Text("y = x^2", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        curve_label.next_to(curve, UP, buff=0.1)

        # 2. Speedometer Setup
        # Base arc
        speedo_arc = Arc(radius=1.5, start_angle=PI, angle=-PI, color=WHITE)
        speedo_ticks = VGroup(*[
            Line(UP * 1.4, UP * 1.5, color=WHITE).rotate(a, about_point=ORIGIN)
            for a in np.linspace(0, PI, 5)
        ])
        speedo_base = Line(LEFT * 1.5, RIGHT * 1.5, color=WHITE)
        speedo_label = Text("Slope Gauge", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        
        speedo_group = VGroup(speedo_arc, speedo_ticks, speedo_base, speedo_label)
        self.place_in_area(speedo_group, "A4", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        speedo_label.next_to(speedo_base, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        speedo_center = speedo_base.get_center()

        # 3. Needle setup
        # Needle starts at the middle (pointing up, representing slope 0)
        needle = Line(speedo_center, speedo_center + UP * 1.3, color="#FF4500", stroke_width=5)
        needle_pivot = Dot(speedo_center, color=WHITE, radius=0.05)

        self.play(
            Create(axes),
            Create(curve),
            Write(curve_label),
            Create(speedo_arc),
            Create(speedo_ticks),
            Create(speedo_base),
            Write(speedo_label),
            Create(needle),
            Create(needle_pivot),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The speedometer needle (#FF4500) rotates based on the curve's current slope.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF4500")

        # Value tracker for x position on curve
        x_tracker = ValueTracker(-1.5)
        
        # Moving dot on curve
        moving_dot = Dot(color="#FF4500").add_updater(
            lambda d: d.move_to(axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), x_tracker.get_value()**2))
        )
        
        # Tangent line (visual shortcut for slope)
        tangent = always_redraw(lambda: TangentLine(curve, alpha=(x_tracker.get_value() + 1.5) / 3, length=2).set_color("#FF4500"))

        # Needle rotation logic: 
        # slope of x^2 is 2x. 
        # We map x in [-1.5, 1.5] to angles on the speedometer.
        # x = -1.5 -> slope = -3 -> angle = PI (Left)
        # x = 0    -> slope = 0  -> angle = PI/2 (Up)
        # x = 1.5  -> slope = 3  -> angle = 0 (Right)
        
        def update_needle(n):
            current_x = x_tracker.get_value()
            slope = 2 * current_x
            # Map slope range roughly [-3, 3] to PI to 0
            angle = PI/2 - np.arctan(slope)
            direction = np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0])
            n.set_points_as_corners([speedo_center, speedo_center + direction * 1.3])

        needle.add_updater(update_needle)
        
        self.add(moving_dot, tangent)
        
        # Animate movement
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(1.5), run_time=6, rate_func=linear)
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(-1.5), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(0), run_time=2, rate_func=smooth)
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Flash the text 'Derivative = Speed of Change' in white across the center.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        
        flash_text = Text("Derivative = Speed of Change", font_size=32, color=WHITE, weight=BOLD)
        self.place_in_area(flash_text, "B2", "E5")
        
        # Add a dark semi-transparent rectangle behind the flash text for readability
        bg_rect = SurroundingRectangle(flash_text, color=BLACK, fill_opacity=0.8, buff=0.3)

        self.play(
            FadeIn(bg_rect),
            Write(flash_text),
            flash_text.animate.scale(1.2),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(flash_text.animate.scale(1/1.2), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)

        # Final cleanup/freeze
        needle.remove_updater(update_needle)
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Mastering Derivatives: Geometric Intuition and Essential Formulas
outline.target_audience: High school students or introductory college calculus students

sections.title: The Foundation: Prerequisite - What is a Slope?
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a constant rate of change using a linear function. Establish that a derivative is simply the 'slope' at a specific point on any curve, moving from average speed to instantaneous speed.
sections.example: A snail named 'Turbo' crawls up a straight plank. If the plank rises 2 meters for every 1 meter of forward movement, the slope (derivative) is a constant 2. Visual: A grid showing a straight line with a 'rise over run' triangle.

sections.title: The Geometric Intuition: Local Linearity
sections.content: Explain that if you zoom in infinitely on any smooth curve, it eventually looks like a straight line. This 'tangent line' represents the derivative at that exact point. Emphasize that the derivative tells us the direction and steepness of the curve's 'micro-moment'.
sections.example: Visualize a magnifying glass zooming into a point on a parabolic rollercoaster track (y = x²). As we zoom in, the curve flattens into a line. This line's slope is our derivative.

sections.title: The Power Rule: The Geometry of Growing Squares
sections.content: Introduce the Power Rule: d/dx(x^n) = nx^(n-1). Instead of just memorizing, visualize x² as a square. When x grows by a tiny bit (dx), the area increases along two sides. Each side has a length of x, hence the '2x'.
sections.example: A 'Shape-Shifting Robot' that is a square of side length 'x'. When it grows slightly, it adds a thin strip to the top and the right. The added area is roughly 2x * dx. Visual: A square expanding with highlighted edges.

sections.title: Trigonometric Derivatives: The Rhythm of the Circle
sections.content: Explain the derivative of sin(x) as cos(x) through a unit circle. If a point moves around a circle at a constant speed, its vertical position is sin(x). Its vertical velocity (the derivative) is its horizontal position, which is cos(x).
sections.example: A rider on a Ferris wheel. When they are at the very side (sin(0)=0), they are moving straight up at maximum speed (cos(0)=1). At the very top (sin(90°)=1), their vertical speed is zero (cos(90°)=0). Visual: A rotating wheel with velocity vectors.

sections.title: Summary: The Speedometer of Change
sections.content: Synthesize the formulas with the geometric intuition. Remind students that formulas are just shortcuts for finding the slope of the 'zoomed-in' line. Highlight that derivatives allow us to predict the future state of dynamic systems.
sections.example: A dashboard display showing a car's position graph (the curve) and its speedometer (the derivative). As the car accelerates, the graph gets steeper and the speedometer needle rises simultaneously. Visual: Side-by-side animation of a curve being drawn and a gauge moving.

This local linearity defines the derivative's value here.

storyboard.title: The Power Rule: The Geometry of Growing Squares
lecture_lines: Imagine a square with side x and area x-squared.
As x grows, thin strips appear on the edges.
A tiny corner piece also forms as it expands.
The two side strips each have an area of x.
The Power Rule proves this growth rate is 2x.

Their vertical position follows a smooth sine wave.
Their vertical speed matches the circle's horizontal cosine.
